findings.title: NudgeStreamer.collectNudge credits the buffer with the amount SENT, not received, against a POOLED per-token balance — one taxed token drains sibling streams and bricks batchMint for every reward token

classification.c4Criterion: C4 Medium - 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted ... with stated assumptions, but external requirements'.
classification.assetImpact: No theft and no economic loss. Two distinct effects, deliberately rated on the availability axis only: (a) CROSS-PAIR CONSUMPTION - pair A's settlement is paid out of the pooled per-token balance that also backs pair B, so B's backing is consumed. Because Phoenix nudge pots are funded by yield on protocol-owned capital, this is MISALLOCATION between two legitimate recipient pots, NOT a value leak, and is expressly not scored as economic loss (repo rule: externally-derived yield is opportunity cost, not loss). (b) AVAILABILITY BRICK - the under-backed pair's pullPendingStream reverts, and because BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint loops pullPendingStream over the entire getNudgeTokens() whitelist inside one transaction (verified at top-level HEAD, BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:527-532), a single tainted token bricks the ENTIRE mint path for every reward token. This is the load-bearing impact and it is a protocol-function failure.
attackPath: 1. Owner whitelists a fee-on-transfer / taxed / reflection token as a nudge token via setNudgeTokenWhitelist (non-obvious footgun; Kendu Inu's real transfer semantics are unverified on-chain).

2. A donor calls collectNudge(batchMinter, token, amount); NudgeStreamer.sol:149-150 does safeTransferFrom then `s.buffer += amount` with no balance-delta measurement, so the credited buffer exceeds actual custody by the tax.
3. A second (batchMinter, token) pair is registered on the SAME token. Custody is pooled per token; the cap in _accrued is per STREAM, so total credited buffers now exceed the single pooled balance.
4. Whichever pair settles first is paid its full over-stated buffer out of the shared balance, consuming the other pair's backing.
5. The later pair's pullPendingStream reverts on insufficient balance.
6. batchMint, which loops pullPendingStream over all whitelisted tokens in one tx, now reverts for ALL reward tokens - the whole mint path is down, not just the tainted reward.
classification.likelihood: medium-low as a trigger, high as a consequence once triggered. There is NO external attacker and no unauthorised actor anywhere in the path; the trigger is an owner whitelisting decision. It is nonetheless a genuine Law-3 footgun rather than trusted-owner noise: a competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised that whitelisting one memecoin bricks minting for every reward token, and the contract's own NatSpec at :193-195 tells them the opposite.
classification.assumptions: (1) A fee-on-transfer / taxed / reflection token is whitelisted as a nudge token. (2) For the cross-pair drain specifically, at least two (batchMinter, token) pairs share one token; the single-pair case yields under-delivery and a stuck residual rather than a revert. (3) FoT is IN SCOPE for this family - the C4 'weird ERC-20 / fee-on-transfer' known-invalid predicate does NOT fire, because phoenix-nft-staking story-022 s4.4 documents FoT explicitly and the defect is a first-party accounting bug in NudgeStreamer.sol, not a request for weird-token support.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner must admit a taxed token through setNudgeTokenWhitelist. No timing, MEV, price or third-party dependency.

findings.severityRationale: MEDIUM, matching the auditor's proposal. Held AT medium from both directions. NOT ESCALATED TO HIGH: nothing is stolen and nothing leaves the protocol perimeter - there is no attacker, no external beneficiary, and the shortfall manifests as a REVERT plus a stranded residual, not as extraction. The cross-pair effect moves value between two legitimate protocol-owned pots, which under this repo's standing rule on externally-derived yield is misallocation and never a value leak. The condition is also owner-reversible (de-whitelist the tainted token, or top the streamer up by the accumulated tax) so the brick is not terminal. NOT DEFLATED TO LOW: the availability failure is PROVEN, not argued - PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevNudgeStreamerFoT.t.sol is 4/4 PASS against the REAL NudgeStreamer (case A over-credit, case B cross-pair drain + revert, case C one tainted token reverts the whole loop, case D the divergence vanishes at feeBps==0). Case D is what makes this reportable rather than theoretical: it proves the only defence in the system - the DeployMocks.s.sol:1661 probe - is VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, since it runs solely against MockKendu and MockPhUSD which are both fee-free, so it cannot fail. There is no on-chain guard anywhere. SEVERITY-RAISING FACTOR: the contract NatSpec at NudgeStreamer.sol:193-195 affirmatively asserts 'The buffer cap guarantees the streamer can never transfer more than it holds' - the guarantee is per-STREAM while custody is POOLED PER-TOKEN, so it is false across pairs. Per this repo's standing principle, falsely-exhaustive documentation raises severity rather than lowering it: it is the reason an operator would never think to check, and it is why this does not settle at Low as a documented design constraint. PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET and verified against top-level submodule HEAD (lib/phoenix-nft-staking/src/NudgeStreamer.sol is byte-identical to the nested pin lib/nft-staking, so this is not a stale-pin artefact).

findings.description: `collectNudge` performs `IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount); s.buffer += amount;` (:149-150) with no balance-delta measurement. The streamer holds a SINGLE POOLED balance per token across every `(batchMinter, token)` pair, while `_settle` caps payouts against the per-stream accounting buffer (`_accrued`, :193-200), not against real custody. The contract NatSpec at :194-196 asserts 'The buffer cap guarantees the streamer can never transfer more than it holds, even if elapsed is large' — that guarantee is PER-STREAM whereas custody is POOLED PER-TOKEN, so it does not hold across pairs. The deploy-script probe at DeployMocks.s.sol:1661 is the only defence anywhere and it is VACUOUS: it runs solely against MockKendu and MockPhUSD, both defined with no transfer fee, so it cannot fail locally. There is no on-chain guard.
findings.impact: For any reward token that is fee-on-transfer, taxed, or reflection-based: (1) the credited buffer immediately exceeds custody; (2) whichever `(batchMinter, token)` pair settles first is paid its full over-stated buffer out of the shared balance, consuming the backing of the other pairs; (3) the later pair's `pullPendingStream` REVERTS on insufficient balance; and (4) because `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint` loops `pullPendingStream` over `getNudgeTokens()` inside one transaction (:539), a single tainted token bricks batchMint for ALL reward tokens — the entire mint path, not just the tainted reward. Kendu Inu is a memecoin whose real transfer semantics are unverified, and MockKendu's own NatSpec states the mock is deliberately fee-free because the streamer assumes exact delivery.
findings.evidence: PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevNudgeStreamerFoT.t.sol — 4/4 PASS against the REAL NudgeStreamer with a 5% fee-on-transfer ERC20. (A) buffer 100,000e18 vs custody 95,000e18. (B) two pairs of the same token: buffers 200,000e18 vs pooled custody 190,000e18; pair A settles and the streamer pays out its full 100,000, leaving 90,000 against pair B's 100,000 claim; B's pullPendingStream reverts. (C) a clean token settles fine in isolation while the tainted token reverts — and batchMint shares one transaction. (D) at feeBps==0 the divergence vanishes entirely, confirming the DeployMocks probe passes vacuously by construction. Also confirmed on the live local chain: streamer balance EXACTLY equals the credited buffer for all three tokens, i.e. the condition under which this finding is invisible.
findings.recommendation: Measure the receipt in `collectNudge`: `uint256 before = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)); safeTransferFrom(...); uint256 received = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)) - before; s.buffer += received;` and recompute the rate from `received`. If fee-on-transfer tokens are intended to be permanently out of scope, add an on-chain probe in `registerStream` (which is already owner-gated and is the natural admission point) rather than relying on a deploy-script assert against a mock that cannot fail. Independently, verify the real Kendu token's transfer semantics on-chain BEFORE `setNudgeTokenWhitelist` on mainnet.

findings.title: BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer is the only one of six streamer setters with no zero-address guard — zeroing it silently strands every accrued stream while batchMint keeps succeeding
findings.severityAgreement: DISAGREE - ESCALATED from proposed low to medium

classification.c4Criterion: C4 Medium - 'Assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted ... with stated assumptions, but external requirements'.
classification.assetImpact: No theft, no economic loss, and expressly NOT scored as a value leak (the nudge pot is funded by yield on protocol-owned capital, so a non-arriving payout is a functional failure, not an economic one). The impact is AVAILABILITY OF A PROMISED PAYOUT: with the streamer zeroed, a qualifying batchMint(26) that should pay 45,045,015 USDC + 5,000e18 phUSD + 50,000e18 Kendu instead pays 189,464 USDC + 0 + 0, and SUCCEEDS - no revert, no distinguishable event. The entire matured pot stays stranded in the streamer. Because pullPendingStream is the ONLY path by which streamed funds reach the batch minter while donors keep pushing INTO the streamer, the divergence grows without bound and is observable only by manually comparing streamer buffers against sink balances.
attackPath: 1. Operator wires the sink using a wrong or placeholder address. The trigger is present IN-REPO, not hypothesised: server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts:131 carries `NudgeStreamer: 0x000...000`, type-indistinguishable from a real address because the ContractAddresses interface is regenerated from ANVIL data with every field a required plain `string` (DEV-06).

2. BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer (top-level HEAD :290-293) accepts address(0) with no guard - unlike all five siblings, which revert (BalancerPoolerV2:247, Uniboost:191, PromotionUniV2_Eth:349, StableYieldAccumulator:514, NudgeRatchet:106). Verified directly at HEAD this run.
3. batchMint gates the whole pullPendingStream loop on `if (_nudgeStreamer != address(0))` (:527), so the streaming leg becomes a silent no-op while the mint itself keeps succeeding.

4. Donors continue to push into the streamer. Every accrued stream strands. Nothing reverts, nothing logs a distinguishable event, and the five loud siblings have taught the operator to expect a revert on a bad address.
classification.likelihood: medium. Requires an operator misstep, but a SPECIFICALLY ENABLED one: the exact wrong value sits in the repo's own mainnet address book today, the type system hides it, and DEV-07 shows the prose in that same file inverts the deployed/not-deployed distinction for four other entries. Detection is manual and comparative, so the window is long.
classification.assumptions: (1) Non-malicious owner throughout - this is rated purely as a Law-3 footgun, never as a malicious-admin vector. (2) The operator wires the streamer to address(0) or to a wrong address, e.g. by sourcing it from mainnet-addresses.ts. (3) The address(0)-as-'streaming-disabled' sentinel is a deliberate and defensible design in isolation; the defect is that the ONE setter in a family of six that accepts the value every sibling rejects also fails SILENTLY.
classification.externalRequirements: An operator mis-wire, plus the absence of a post-deploy assertion. DeployMocks post-asserts only the SYA leg (:1129) of seven setNudgeStreamer calls (see DEV-09), so the runbook does not catch it either.

findings.severityRationale: ESCALATED to MEDIUM against the auditor's proposed Low. Escalation is justified on five independent grounds, and I am deliberately explicit because overstatement is a documented rejection cause for this pipeline. (1) PROVEN, NOT ARGUED: PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevStreamerWiring.t.sol is 2/2 PASS run --fork-url against the live chain; test_zeroAddressGuardAsymmetry shows all six donors return ok==false while BatchNFTMinterMultiToken returns ok==true, and test_zeroedSinkStrandsAccruedStreams shows the SAME batchMint(26) silently paying 189,464 instead of the full pot. The magnitude is measured, not estimated. (2) THE DEFECT IS THE SILENCE, NOT THE SENTINEL. A sentinel that disables a feature is fine; a sentinel that is accepted by exactly one of six sibling setters, whose five peers all revert loudly, actively INVERTS the intuition the operator has been trained to hold. That is the textbook Law-3 test - a competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised - and Law 3 requires such a footgun to be classified BY THE IMPACT IT UNLOCKS, not auto-downgraded to a centralization/QA note. The impact unlocked is the unbounded non-arrival of the entire nudge pot. (3) THE TRIGGER IS LIVE IN-REPO. This is not 'an operator might one day fat-finger an address'. DEV-06 puts a 0x0 NudgeStreamer placeholder into mainnet-addresses.ts that the type system cannot distinguish from a real address, and DEV-07 shows the surrounding prose already inverts real-vs-placeholder for four other entries. The C4 'user input mistake' exclusion does not fire, because the repo itself supplies the wrong input. (4) FAMILY PRECEDENT. The identical class - a sentinel/zero collaborator making the value leg a silent no-op while the main call keeps succeeding - was filed in yield-claim-nft as c91bef813d (M-04) at MEDIUM, and the owner triaged it 'Owner ack - WILL FIX (revert on unwired dispatch)'. That fix landed on ATokenDispatcherV2; BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer never received the fail-closed treatment. Rating the same class Low here would be inconsistent with the family's own accepted precedent. yield-claim-nft 563df2e64a (L-09) is the precedent for keeping a reborn instance open on its own rather than folding it under a fixed sibling. (5) PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET, on the live BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, with no compensating on-chain or runbook control. NOT ESCALATED FURTHER TO HIGH: nothing is stolen, no attacker exists, the funds remain in the streamer rather than leaving the protocol, and re-pointing setNudgeStreamer to the correct address restores the pull path - the condition is recoverable once detected. It also requires an operator misstep, which bars the 'no hand-wavy hypotheticals' High bar. Medium is the ceiling this evidence supports. SCOPE DISCIPLINE - DO NOT CONFLATE: the adjacent _dispatch path is NOT part of this finding and is NOT part of the escalation basis. There a DonationSkipped event IS emitted and USDS re-sweeps, making that path bounded QUIETNESS with no value consequence. The escalation rests solely on the setNudgeStreamer leg, which is silent AND strands.
findings.classifierNotes: NOT related on root cause to phoenix-nft-staking 858e9e807a (H-01, wont-fix): that is the value-blind nudge GATE which OVER-pays the pot; DEV-03 STRANDS it - economically the opposite direction. The 858e9e80 wont-fix is NOT cited against this finding. Minimum remediation: emit a distinct NudgeStreamingDisabled event, or split disable from misconfigure via setNudgeStreamingEnabled(bool) + require non-zero; and post-assert `batchMinter.nudgeStreamer() == <expected>` in the mainnet script.
findings.description: All six donor contracts reject `setNudgeStreamer(address(0))` with an explicit guard — BalancerPoolerV2.sol:247, Uniboost.sol:191, NudgeRatchet.sol:106, PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol:349, StableYieldAccumulator.sol:514. `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer` (:299-302) has none, because address(0) is its deliberate 'streaming disabled' sentinel: `batchMint` gates the whole `pullPendingStream` loop on `if (_nudgeStreamer != address(0))` (:538). The sentinel design is defensible in isolation; the hazard is that it is the ONE setter in a family of six that accepts the value every sibling rejects, and its failure mode is silent while every sibling's is a loud revert.
findings.impact: An operator wiring the sink from a wrong or placeholder address (see DEV-06) gets no error and no event distinguishable from a normal reconfiguration. batchMint continues to succeed. Every accrued stream stays stranded in the streamer and the batcher is paid only whatever was already sitting in the sink.
